DOCUMENT:
Vendor Comparison: Standard Parcel Delivery Contract
Larkspur Home, Operations, June 2026

1. Purpose
Our contract with our current standard-delivery carrier ends on 30 September 2026. This paper compares three shortlisted carriers and recommends which should carry our standard (two-to-four-day) parcels from October.

2. Volumes and requirements
We dispatch an average of 42,000 standard parcels a month: about 70% weigh under 2 kg (cushions, textiles, small homeware) and 30% weigh 2 to 10 kg (lamps, mirrors, small furniture). Our requirements are on-time delivery of at least 95%, a damage rate below 0.5%, full tracking, and a returns service.

Damage and loss matter to us commercially. Each damaged or lost parcel costs us on average £48 in replacement stock, return shipping and customer service time, and damaged items are the most common cause of one-star reviews.

3. Trial
Between 1 April and 31 May 2026, each shortlisted carrier delivered a share of our orders, allocated at random by the warehouse management system, about 5,000 parcels per carrier. We measured on-time delivery against the promised date, damage reported by customers within 14 days, and lost parcels.

Table 1. Prices and trial performance
Carrier | Price, under 2 kg | Price, 2-10 kg | On-time delivery | Damage rate | Lost per 10,000 parcels
SwiftDrop | £3.10 | £4.60 | 96.2% | 0.4% | 3
ParcelLine | £2.85 | £4.95 | 93.1% | 0.9% | 8
Meridian | £3.30 | £4.40 | 97.5% | 0.3% | 2

On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial, and all three offer full tracking and a returns service.

4. Cost comparison
Applying our 70/30 weight mix, the average cost per parcel is £3.55 for SwiftDrop, £3.48 for ParcelLine and £3.63 for Meridian. On 42,000 parcels a month, the monthly cost would be £149,100 for SwiftDrop, £146,160 for ParcelLine and £152,460 for Meridian. ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop and £6,300 a month against Meridian, or between about £35,000 and £76,000 a year.

5. Customer contact
"Where is my order?" contacts are our largest single category of customer service enquiry. During the trial, ParcelLine deliveries generated 6 such contacts per 1,000 parcels, compared with 11 for SwiftDrop and 10 for Meridian. ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts, and at an average handling cost of £3.20 per contact this would save about £670 a month at our volumes. From 1 May, ParcelLine parcels also carried our new proactive delivery-day text message, which we were testing on one carrier before rolling it out.

6. Other considerations
All three carriers can collect from our warehouse daily at 6 pm. ParcelLine and SwiftDrop offer a 12-month contract; Meridian requires 24 months. SwiftDrop and Meridian have both handled our peak-season volumes for other retailers of similar size, while ParcelLine's references were mainly from fashion retailers with lighter parcels.

All three carriers integrate with our warehouse management system through standard interfaces, and none would require changes to our packing process or labelling. Each offers recipients a delivery-preference service to nominate a safe place or a neighbour, and each provides proof-of-delivery photographs, which our customer service team has found useful in resolving disputes.

7. Recommendation
ParcelLine offers the lowest delivery cost, met our service requirements in the trial and reduces customer contacts through its tracking app. We recommend awarding the standard parcel contract to ParcelLine for 12 months from 1 October 2026, saving up to £76,000 a year against the alternatives.

KEY (three known flaws):
1. [misread_evidence] at: "On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial" -- Table 1 shows ParcelLine's on-time delivery was 93.1%, below the 95% requirement. The claim (and the recommendation that ParcelLine 'met our service requirements') misreads the table; ParcelLine's 0.9% damage rate also fails the stated 0.5% requirement.
2. [unsupported_causal] at: "ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts" -- The document states that from 1 May ParcelLine parcels alone also carried the new proactive delivery-day text message. That concurrent intervention confounds the comparison, so the lower contact rate cannot be attributed to ParcelLine's tracking app.
3. [missing_consideration] at: "ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop" -- The cost comparison ignores the stated £48 cost of each damaged or lost parcel. ParcelLine's damage and loss rates (0.9% and 8 per 10,000) versus SwiftDrop's (0.4% and 3 per 10,000) imply about 231 extra problem parcels a month (about £11,100), far exceeding the £2,940 price saving; ParcelLine is likely the most expensive option overall.

REVIEW:
This review finds that the recommendation doesn't follow from the document's own data. The price arithmetic is correct, and ParcelLine is the cheapest on price alone. But:

1. **ParcelLine failed two of the four stated requirements in the trial.** Its on-time delivery was **93.1%**, below the 95% threshold; the paper and the cover note both say all three carriers cleared it. Its damage rate was **0.9%**, nearly double the 0.5% maximum.
2. **Once damage and loss are costed, ParcelLine is the most expensive option.** At the paper's own £48 per damaged or lost parcel, ParcelLine costs roughly **£75,000–£90,000 a year more** than SwiftDrop or Meridian. That's before the reputational cost of one-star reviews.
3. **The customer-contact advantage can't be credited to ParcelLine's app.** ParcelLine parcels alone carried your new proactive delivery-day text from 1 May, which is half the trial.

On the evidence in the paper, **SwiftDrop** looks like the strongest choice. It meets every requirement, has the lowest total cost, offers the same 12-month term, and has peak-season experience.

## 1. ParcelLine doesn't meet the requirements

| Requirement | SwiftDrop | ParcelLine | Meridian |
|---|---|---|---|
| On-time ≥ 95% | 96.2% ✓ | **93.1% ✗** | 97.5% ✓ |
| Damage < 0.5% | 0.4% ✓ | **0.9% ✗** | 0.3% ✓ |
| Full tracking | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Returns service | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

Section 3's sentence "On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers" is contradicted by Table 1, directly above it. Section 7's "met our service requirements in the trial" is also wrong, and so is the cover note's "not trading reliability for price."

With about 5,000 parcels per carrier, these gaps are unlikely to be noise:
- Damage at 0.9% vs 0.4% is roughly 45 vs 20 damaged parcels, which is statistically clear.
- On-time at 93.1% vs 96.2% is a gap of about 150 parcels.

## 2. Total cost, including damage and loss

The paper sets out the £48 cost per damaged or lost parcel in Section 2 but never applies it. At 42,000 parcels a month:

| Monthly | SwiftDrop | ParcelLine | Meridian |
|---|---|---|---|
| Delivery charges | £149,100 | £146,160 | £152,460 |
| Damaged parcels | 168 | 378 | 126 |
| Lost parcels | ~13 | ~34 | ~8 |
| Damage and loss at £48 | £8,669 | £19,757 | £6,451 |
| "Where is my order?" contacts at £3.20 | £1,478 | £806 | £1,344 |
| **Total** | **£159,247** | **£166,723** | **£160,255** |

**Annual difference vs ParcelLine:**
- SwiftDrop: about **£89,700 cheaper**.
- Meridian: about **£77,600 cheaper**.

This table even gives ParcelLine full credit for its lower contact rate, which is overstated (see the next section). Without that credit, the gap is wider. The ranking also doesn't depend on the lost-parcel figures: damage alone produces it.

The table leaves out the cost of late deliveries, such as complaints, refunds and repeat purchases lost, and the effect of one-star reviews. Both would count further against ParcelLine.

The delivery-price arithmetic in Section 4 is all correct: £3.55 / £3.48 / £3.63 per parcel, the monthly totals, and annual savings of £35,280 and £75,600. It just isn't the whole cost.

## 3. The customer-contact comparison is confounded

- ParcelLine had 6 contacts per 1,000 parcels, against 11 for SwiftDrop and 10 for Meridian.
- But from 1 May, **only ParcelLine parcels carried the new proactive delivery-day text.** Proactive notifications are designed precisely to reduce "where is my order?" contacts.
- ParcelLine also had the *worst* on-time rate. Fewer chasing contacts despite more late parcels points strongly to the text message as the cause, not the app.

So "ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts" isn't supported. To salvage the evidence:
- Compare **April only**, before the text started, if the data can be split by month.
- Otherwise, describe the result as inconclusive.

Since you plan to roll the text out to whichever carrier you choose, the eventual contact saving will probably go to the winner regardless.

The £670/month figure is also the saving against SwiftDrop only: 5 fewer contacts per 1,000 × 42,000 × £3.20 = £672. Against Meridian it's about £538.

## 4. Peak-season risk

- The trial ran April–May, and the contract starts on 1 October, straight into peak.
- SwiftDrop and Meridian have handled peak volumes for retailers your size. ParcelLine's references are mainly fashion retailers with lighter parcels.
- 30% of your volume is 2–10 kg lamps, mirrors and small furniture. These are fragile and heavy, which is exactly where the damage rate matters.

This counts against ParcelLine and should be named as a risk if it remains under consideration.

## 5. Smaller points

- **Lost-parcel rates rest on tiny counts.** At about 5,000 parcels, 2–8 per 10,000 means 1–4 actual parcels. SwiftDrop's 3 per 10,000 implies 1.5 parcels at exactly 5,000, so the sample sizes evidently differed. Give the actual counts, and don't lean on these rates for decisions. Damage is the meaningful measure.
- **Contract term.** The 12-month term is a fair advantage over Meridian's 24 months, but SwiftDrop offers 12 months too, so it doesn't distinguish ParcelLine.
- **Tracking.** All three offer full tracking. If ParcelLine's app is genuinely better, show evidence other than the contact rate.

## 6. What holds up

- **The trial design is good.** Random allocation by the warehouse system, about 5,000 parcels each, and measures that match the requirements make this a fair head-to-head, as the cover note says.
- **The requirements are clear,** and setting the £48 cost per incident in advance is exactly the right number to have.
- **The price arithmetic is correct.**
- **Section 6** is useful context: integration, collection times, proof-of-delivery photos and references.

## Suggested changes before this goes forward

1. Correct the on-time statement, and show which carriers meet each requirement.
2. Add a total-cost table including damage and loss at £48 per incident.
3. Re-run the contact comparison on April data only, or remove the attribution to ParcelLine's app.
4. Add peak-season risk to the assessment.
5. Revisit the recommendation. On these figures SwiftDrop leads: all requirements met, lowest total cost, 12-month term and peak experience. Meridian is the best performer if you'd accept a 24-month term for slightly higher cost. If there's a strong reason to prefer ParcelLine, the paper needs to state it and explain how its damage and on-time performance would be brought within requirements.

The trial was well designed, and it answered the question. The answer just isn't the one the recommendation gives.
